name: Summary page polish: notes, sidebar, header

pr.title: Polish the summary page's notes, sidebar, and header
pr.head: a73fb262cc16156bf1053ab08d59e83f3e57ee7b

summary: A summary page is the guided review page that project summary publish puts on a repository's Projector site. Each file on the page is a card: a header, an optional one-line description, the notes about the file, and then its diff as one table per hunk. A note is a reviewer's remark, tagged context, verified, or concern. A note can sit under one line of the diff, at the top of a card about the whole file, or at the top of a section about several files. The sidebar on the left shows the pull request's stack, the projects it changes, the sections, and the published versions of the summary.

Notes under a line already render as rows of the diff table, with the tag in the line-number gutter and the text where the code starts. The other notes were bulleted lists, so their tags and text lined up with nothing in the diffs. This pull request makes the top notes on a card the same kind of row, in a small table that shares the diff's columns. A section's notes get the same layout as grid rows, with the tag in a column as wide as the diff's gutter. Every note on the page now starts its text at the same distance from the edge of its box.
It also reworks the sidebar, the header, and the overview:

• A stack of one. The sidebar lists every pull request in a stack, one row each, with the current one highlighted. A pull request with no stack showed only its title in grey. It now shows the same list with one highlighted row. The build's data does not change: only the page draws the row.
  • Projects as rows. The projects a pull request changes were a line of links reading "Projects: …" below the stack. They are now rows above the stack, styled like the stack's but a step larger, at 13.5px with 9px of padding above and below and 10px on the right, with each title spanning its row. Neither kind of row carries a tooltip repeating its title.
  • Credit and versions on the last row. The "Generated by Projector" credit moves from below the sidebar's box into the box's last row. A history icon at the right of that row opens the list of published versions below it. The icon's tooltip and accessible name read "Versions (N)", and the current version is marked with the secondary surface colour. With one version, the row holds only the credit.
  • Plainer links. The page header's Conversation, Files, and Compare links are spaced apart with a gap instead of dot separators, and are no longer underlined. The sidebar's Overview and Files links share one line, sitting directly on the divider below them, and the divider that separated them from the stack above is gone.
  • More room in rows. Note rows get 13px of padding above and below their text instead of 5px, and the sidebar's stack rows get 8px instead of 3px.
  • Notes, and no reading guide. A section's list of notes is headed Notes, not Review notes. The "How to read this" paragraph that every page appended to its "What this PR does" card is gone, so the card holds only what the summary wrote.

cards.title: Review status at this head
cards.html:
• The first Projector review asked for one change: a line in docs/cli.md that the edit left unwrapped. The author rewrapped it, and later reviews found it fixed.
  • The author took the first review's suggestion to drop notesList's unused class parameter, and rewrote the pull request's description to match the change, which later reviews had suggested.
  • Every review from 965ed38 on, this head included, is clean. At this head the repository's gate passes: the site's type check and lint, the build (which reproduced the committed JavaScript exactly), all 506 unit tests, project check, and both plugin validations.
  • The sidebar rows dropped their title tooltips on purpose. A row's title is clamped to three lines, so a title longer than about 85 characters is cut, and the reader follows the link to read it in full.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Card: one file's block on the summary page, rendered by renderFile.
  • Top notes: the notes on a whole file, with no line. The code calls them loose.
  • Note row: a tr.noterow, with the tag in the gutter cell td.ngut and the text in td.nte.
  • Stack: the chain of pull requests whose bases are each other's heads. The build stores it as data.stack, empty for a pull request that stands alone.
  • Section notes: the notes on a whole section, drawn by notesList in a box headed Notes.

groups.title: The page renderer
groups.kicker: Notes line up with the diff's columns, the sidebar gets project rows, a one-row stack, and a shared last row, and the header and overview get plainer.
intro: The summary renderer, site/src/summary.ts, builds the whole page in the browser from the summary's data. renderFile draws one card per file. Before this change it drew a note under a line as a table row inside the diff, and drew the top notes through notesList, the same bulleted list a section uses for its own notes.

Now renderFile has one function, noteRow, that turns any note into a table row. The diff's rows call it for notes under a line, and the top notes go through it into a separate table placed above the diff. That table gets the same class and the same <colgroup> as the diff's hunk tables, so its gutter is exactly as wide as theirs.

A section's notes stay a list, but each item is now a three-column grid: the tag, right-aligned in a 92px column, then the text, then a concern's checkbox. The diff's gutter is also 92px wide, two 46px columns or one 92px column, so a section's note text starts where a file's note text does. The Notes heading is inset 8px from the box's edge, as the diff's cells are from a file card's.

In the sidebar, projectsList now draws the projects as a ul.stack.projects placed before the stack. renderPage moves the credit into the box, in a .navfoot row that also holds the versions toggle from headsList. The header's links drop their dot separators for a flex gap, and renderOverview no longer appends the reading guide. The stylesheet drops the rules for the old .prmeta line, the old .prtitle title, the versions chevron, and the guide's .chip.inline chips.

checks.text: The compiled site/assets/summary.js is the TypeScript's build output and ships with the change. Rebuilding it at this head produced no difference.

files.note: Adds noteRow and the top-notes table in renderFile, reorders section notes, draws projects as sidebar rows, makes stackList fall back to a one-row stack, moves the credit and the versions icon into the box's last row, and drops the reading guide.

checks.text: A section's concern checkbox moves after the text. The checkbox handler still marks box.closest('li, tr'), so a checked concern dims its row. No CSS or script reads the removed <span class="nbox"> placeholder. I traced both.
A concern note's checkbox is keyed by the file's path, the same scope the top-notes list used at the base, so a concern a reader already checked stays checked. I traced it in the code.
The top table holds no tr.add, tr.del, or tr.ctx rows and no .src spans, so syntax highlighting and token marking, which read only those, leave it alone. I traced highlightFile and the token marker.
The table keeps the fnotes class, so the stylesheet's rules for collapsed and reviewed files still remove its border and hide it.
The card ends after the summary's own paragraphs. A summary that relied on the page to explain the note kinds now has to say it in its overview.
The label is built from a number only, so it needs no escaping in the attribute.

stackList uses data.stack only when it lists two or more pull requests. Otherwise it draws one current row from the pull request itself. The current row returns before it reads url, so the empty url is never used. A test checks the rendered row.
Each project URL and title goes through esc, as the old .prmeta links did. The row has no title tooltip, so a title past the three-line clamp is cut.
The links now sit side by side with no text between them. The stylesheet's flex gap on .top .sub spaces them, so a page without the stylesheet shows them run together.

.navfoot is positioned, so the versions toggle's absolute position is measured from this row and scrolls with the box. A closed details adds no height, since its list is its only in-flow content. A test checks this row with two versions and with one.

files.note: Styles section notes as gutter-aligned rows, lets the diff's note-row rules style the top notes, adds project rows and the last-row layout, spaces the header and sidebar links with gaps, widens row padding, and drops unused rules.

checks.text: The window-height limit moves from .layout > .side to .side .nav, the box that now holds the credit. The site's own pages load this stylesheet, but their nav.side contains no .nav element, so this rule does not reach them. I checked the markup in site/src/site.ts.
This rule outranks the shared row rule, so only project rows take the larger type. Its 6px left padding matches the shared rule's, so a project title starts where a stack row's number does.

This rule is more specific than .prblock > :first-child, which zeroes the first child's top margin, so it wins. It applies only when the projects list leads the block, which renderPage always does when there are projects.
The new rules select .notes li. The file header's note badge is a span.badge.notes with no list items, so these rules leave it alone.
This padding applies to every note row in a diff, both under a line and at the top of a card.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: Node-rendered tests cover the new markup, and the CLI reference names the stack of one.
intro: FileHeaderTests in tests/test_site.py builds a summary and renders it with the compiled script under node. One test gives a file a note on the whole file and the section a note of its own, and checks the markup of both. Other tests check the one-row stack, the project rows before the stack, the versions icon and the shared last row with two versions and with one, and an overview card that holds only the summary's text. They skip when node is missing. SummarySidebarTests reads the stylesheet and checks where the window-height limit and the scroll now sit.
docs/cli.md describes the site's sidebar, and gains a clause saying that a pull request with no stack is a stack of one, with its own row highlighted.

checks.text: The expected markup pins the exact column group: two lncol columns for a file with both sides.
